title: Lower the core side exponent from 400 to 80 (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4481 leaves HALO's core side `L = 2^{ceil(400 log2 p)}` in place. The volume bound has two sparse powers. Both are negative for group exponents `ε, β < 1` when `A = p^{48}` and `L ≥ p^{400}`. What is the smallest integer `C` that still does this when `A = p^{26}`?

## Result

With `A = p^{26}` and `L ≥ p^C`, the powers are `ε + β + 78 - C` and `ε + 28 - C`. Both are negative for every `ε < 1` and `β < 1` precisely when `C ≥ 80`. At `ε = β = 3/4`, the exponent 79 gives `1/2`. The second power is negative as soon as `C ≥ 29`, so the first power is the binding one.

The same 80 gives `p^{80} > 4 p^{26}` for every integer `p ≥ 2`, and `g A/L` has exponent `-53` when `g ≤ p`. The written 400 still works and is larger. A uniform slack of 1 below zero needs 81; 80 is the smallest integer that makes both powers strictly negative.

**Claim type:** exponent comparison for the sparse volume. **No new κ.** The agreement distance `p^{26}` stays a hypothesis. The tensor error `g p^{10 g} exp(-p^2)` is not retuned, and the #4100 notes are unchanged.
